newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to remove import tariffs on 10 raw materials.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to remove import tariffs on 10 raw materials.

text.p: South Korea plans to remove import tariffs on 10 raw materials from the current one percent to two percent effective from December, the Ministry of Finance and Economy said on Thursday.
But the exact date will be announced later, a ministry statement said.
The plan was in line with the government's drive to enhance companies' competitiveness, the statement said.
The 10 items are ores and concentrates for eight metallic items -- copper, lead, zinc, aluminium, zirconium, molybdenum, manganese and chrome -- and ferrous waste/scrap and wool.
South Korea wholly or heavily depends on imports for these items, it said.
The ministry expects the removal of tariffs to result in bringing down the country's producer price index growth by 0.3 of a basis point, it said.
In calendar 1995, South Korea's imports of these 10 items totalled $2.2 billion, the statement said.
In June, import tariffs were also removed on six other raw materials -- bituminous coal, lumber, iron ore, cotton, rubber and pig iron.
